AASTA HANSTEEN.label: Gas turbine
AASTA HANSTEEN.source_title: Equinor – Aasta Hansteen – technical safety and process safety
AASTA HANSTEEN.evidence: Havtil's 2025 audit identifies the turbine system serving Aasta Hansteen's main power, consistent with the official development report's specification of local gas-turbine electricity generation rather than power from shore.

ALVHEIM.label: Gas turbine
ALVHEIM.source_title: Simultaneous Faults on the 11 kV System of an Offshore FPSO Vessel
ALVHEIM.evidence: A technical paper co-authored by Alvheim's then-operator Marathon documents two 23.76 MW gas-turbine generator packages on Alvheim FPSO; the field remains in production through that FPSO and has ongoing fuel-gas consumption.

BALDER.label: Gas + diesel generation
BALDER.evidence: Vår Energi's 2025 Balder-area emissions report identifies offshore power generation from gas and diesel, including gas turbines on Jotun FPSO and Ringhorne and diesel engines on Balder FPU.

BRAGE.label: Gas turbine
BRAGE.evidence: OKEA reports that Brage's turbines normally combust gas for power generation, with diesel used only during limited abnormal operating conditions; the proposed direct-connected wind project was not approved.

DRAUGEN.label: Gas turbine
DRAUGEN.evidence: Operator OKEA states that associated gas is currently used for power generation; its electrification material says power from shore will replace the platform's current gas-turbine generation, with the project still under development in 2026.

EDVARD GRIEG.label: Power from shore
EDVARD GRIEG.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
EDVARD GRIEG.evidence: SODIR states that Edvard Grieg has run on power transmitted via Johan Sverdrup and the Utsira High area solution since 2022, covering the field's entire power need.

EKOFISK.label: Gas turbine
EKOFISK.evidence: ConocoPhillips reports 900.09 GWh of self-produced mechanical/electrical energy at Ekofisk in 2024, zero electricity imported from shore, offshore wind, or another field, and fuel-gas combustion in SAC/DLE turbines.

ELDFISK.label: Gas turbine + waste heat
ELDFISK.evidence: ConocoPhillips' 2024 field report says Eldfisk 2/7 E uses gas-turbine exhaust heat to generate electricity and supplies the Eldfisk complex; its subsea cable also links the gas-powered Greater Ekofisk grid.

EMBLA.label: Host · gas power
EMBLA.evidence: Embla receives electricity by cable through Eldfisk 2/7 S; ConocoPhillips states that S is supplied from Eldfisk 2/7 E, whose generation is gas-based with gas- and steam-turbine electrical capacity.

FRIGG.label: Gas turbine
FRIGG.source_title: TCP2 Operations Manual, Volume 1 — Electrical and Communication Systems
FRIGG.evidence: Frigg's operating manual states that field-wide power was generated by two 16 MW turbine-driven generators on TCP2; the turbo-generators were dual-fuelled with gas or diesel, with small diesel standby units.

FRØY.label: Frigg host · gas turbine
FRØY.source_title: TCP2 Operations Manual, Volume 1 – General Platform, Part 2
FRØY.evidence: The TCP2 manual documents a 5.5/22 kV transformer feeding the Frøy wellhead platform and states that TCP2's dual-fuel generator sets normally ran on gas.

GINA KROG.label: Power from shore
GINA KROG.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
GINA KROG.evidence: Gina Krog has received power via Johan Sverdrup's Utsira High area solution since 2023, covering the field's entire power need.

GJØA.label: Shore power + gas turbine
GJØA.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
GJØA.evidence: Gjøa has been partly electrified from shore since startup in 2010, while a local gas turbine drives gas export and supplies process heat through heat recovery.

GLITNE.label: Onboard gas power
GLITNE.evidence: Equinor states that Petrojarl I was fitted with two specially built generators to produce electricity from Glitne's associated gas.

GOLIAT.label: Power from shore
GOLIAT.source_title: Vår Energi is securing higher production for longer from the Goliat field
GOLIAT.evidence: Vår Energi states in its 15 April 2026 Goliat Gas Export announcement that Goliat is fully electrified with power from shore.

GRANE.label: Gas turbine
GRANE.evidence: Grane's approved design generates power with three gas turbines, and Equinor confirms the proposed Grane-Balder power-from-shore project was discontinued in 2026, so gas-turbine generation remains the current supply.

GUDRUN.label: Power from shore
GUDRUN.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
GUDRUN.evidence: SODIR states that Gudrun has operated with power from shore since the Utsira High-to-Sleipner connection entered service in 2024.

GULLFAKS.label: Wind + gas turbines
GULLFAKS.source_title: Emissions to air — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
GULLFAKS.evidence: Hywind Tampen supplies roughly 35% of Gullfaks and Snorre's annual electricity demand; the facilities supplement this variable wind supply with gas-turbine generation.

GYDA.label: Gas turbine
GYDA.source_title: Opportunity 41: More efficient turbine operation on Gyda
GYDA.evidence: Offshore Norge records Gyda operating one turbine on fuel gas and using a second turbine intermittently on diesel when required.

HANZ.label: Power from shore
HANZ.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
HANZ.evidence: Hanz is supplied through the shore-powered Ivar Aasen installation; its direct accounting and navigation relationship remains Hanz to Ivar Aasen.

HEIDRUN.label: Gas turbine
HEIDRUN.evidence: Equinor's 2025 field report records 154.4 million Sm³ of fuel gas used by SAC and DLE turbines, says electricity is mainly generated by generator turbines, and reports no imported electricity from shore, wind, or another field.

HEIMDAL.label: Gas turbine
HEIMDAL.evidence: The Heimdal main generator was a dry-gas-fuelled gas turbine, with the older KG5 units retained as backup generation.

HOD.label: Power from shore
HOD.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
HOD.evidence: SODIR states that Hod's wellhead platform receives electricity from Valhall, whose entire power need is supplied from shore.

HULDRA.label: Diesel generators
HULDRA.source_title: St.prp. nr. 8 (1998–99) — Development and operation of Huldra
HULDRA.evidence: The approved development description says Huldra's electrical demand was supplied by diesel-driven generators; remote control from Veslefrikk did not include a power cable.

IVAR AASEN.label: Power from shore
IVAR AASEN.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
IVAR AASEN.evidence: The Directorate says Ivar Aasen has run on power from shore via the Utsira High area solution since it became operational in 2022, covering the platform through its cable from Edvard Grieg.

JOHAN CASTBERG.label: Gas turbines
JOHAN CASTBERG.source_title: Prop. 80 S (2017–2018): Development and operation of Johan Castberg
JOHAN CASTBERG.evidence: The approved development uses two 33 MW low-NOx gas turbines on the FPSO for electrical power, plus a separate 40 MW gas turbine mechanically driving gas injection.

JOHAN SVERDRUP.label: Power from shore
JOHAN SVERDRUP.source_title: Developing the largest oil producer on the Norwegian continental shelf
JOHAN SVERDRUP.evidence: Equinor states that Johan Sverdrup is powered by electricity from shore; the operator's 2025 field update confirms this remains the field's operating power supply.

JOTUN.label: Gas turbine
JOTUN.evidence: Vår Energi's 2025 emissions report lists gas-fired turbines on the redeployed Jotun FPSO and records accredited exhaust measurements from those turbines.

KNARR.label: Gas turbine
KNARR.source_title: Petroleumstilsynet audit of Teekay's barrier management on Petrojarl Knarr (2016)
KNARR.evidence: The 2016 Petroleum Safety Authority audit of Petrojarl Knarr explicitly describes gas-fired power generation and discusses fuel-gas piping to the turbines.

KRISTIN.label: Gas turbine
KRISTIN.source_title: PUD/PAD for Kristin — Environmental impact assessment, part 2
KRISTIN.evidence: Equinor's approved development assessment specifies two LM2500+ gas turbines for electrical generation; Equinor's current electrification page says the proposed Halten partial-electrification project covering Kristin was discontinued in October 2025.

KVITEBJØRN.label: Gas turbine
KVITEBJØRN.source_title: Equinor annual report for the Kvitebjørn field, 2021
KVITEBJØRN.evidence: Equinor reports that Kvitebjørn produced its electricity mainly with generator turbines fired by gas, imported no electricity from shore, wind or another field, and exported power to Valemon.

MARTIN LINGE.label: Power from shore
MARTIN LINGE.source_title: Field: MARTIN LINGE — Norwegian Offshore Directorate Factpages
MARTIN LINGE.evidence: SODIR's field description, updated 20 February 2026, states that the Martin Linge installation is supplied with power from shore.

MURCHISON.label: Gas turbine
MURCHISON.evidence: The government-approved operator programme records fuel gas imported from the NLGP network to the Murchison platform; facility records identify gas-turbine electricity generation.

NJORD.label: Gas turbine
NJORD.source_title: Njord field cutting 130 000 tonnes of CO2 emissions per year from 2027
NJORD.evidence: Equinor identifies two existing gas turbines as Njord A's main power source; the approved shore-power conversion remained an in-execution future project in 2026, with no commissioning announcement found by 3 August.

NORNE.label: Gas turbine
NORNE.evidence: The 2024 field report says Norne FPSO generated its electricity mainly with generator turbines, imported no electricity from shore, wind, or another field, and burned fuel gas in SAC and DLE turbines.

OSEBERG.label: Gas turbine
OSEBERG.evidence: Oseberg is currently powered by its offshore gas-turbine system; the planned shore-power cable is not yet installed or operational.

OSEBERG SØR.label: Gas turbine
OSEBERG SØR.evidence: Oseberg Sør's installed generation is gas-turbine based; Equinor says its partial shore-power conversion remains in execution and has been postponed to late 2027, so gas turbines are the operational 2026 source.

OSEBERG ØST.label: Gas turbine
OSEBERG ØST.source_title: Equinor — Oseberg Øst decommissioning impact assessment
OSEBERG ØST.evidence: Equinor states that field gas fuels platform power generation and that shutdown timing depends on gas availability; diesel can supplement it, while SODIR's 2026 field status confirms produced gas still supplies the platform generator.

SKARV.label: Gas turbines
SKARV.source_title: Aker BP 2024 CDP Climate Change Questionnaire
SKARV.evidence: Aker BP states that the Skarv FPSO relies on three turbines for operational power and describes its controls as gas-turbine optimization.

SLEIPNER VEST.label: Partial shore power
SLEIPNER VEST.source_title: Reducing emissions from Sleipner and Gudrun
SLEIPNER VEST.evidence: Sleipner Vest is operated through the Sleipner field centre, which Equinor says has received onshore power since 24 March 2024 and operates partly on shore power while a Sleipner A gas turbine remains as backup.

SLEIPNER ØST.label: Shore power + gas
SLEIPNER ØST.source_title: Norwegian Offshore Directorate — Fields with power to shore
SLEIPNER ØST.evidence: Sleipner has received power from shore via Gina Krog since 2024, while some power is still generated by gas turbines.

SNORRE.label: Wind + gas turbines
SNORRE.evidence: Hywind Tampen supplies Snorre A and B with about 35% of annual electricity demand; platform gas turbines provide the balance and full backup when wind is insufficient.

STATFJORD.label: Gas turbine
STATFJORD.evidence: The 2024 field report says gas turbines generate most energy in normal operation across Statfjord A, B and C; Statfjord C's planned 2026 waste-heat steam system is not shore power.

TAMBAR.label: Ula · gas turbine
TAMBAR.source_title: Aker BP CDP 2024 Climate Change Questionnaire
TAMBAR.evidence: Tambar is a remotely controlled tie-back to Ula, while Aker BP's recent climate reporting explicitly describes optimizing turbine power consumption on Ula; Tambar therefore receives host-supplied gas-turbine power.

TOR.label: Ekofisk · host power
TOR.source_title: Field: TOR — Norwegian Offshore Directorate FactPages
TOR.evidence: SODIR describes Tor II as two subsea templates tied back to the Ekofisk Centre, where the well stream is processed; the redeveloped field therefore has no separate forward fuel boundary.

TROLL.label: Power from shore
TROLL.source_title: Field: TROLL — Norwegian Offshore Directorate FactPages
TROLL.evidence: Troll A receives power from shore; Troll B and Troll C have operated partly with power from shore since 2024.

ULA.label: Gas turbine
ULA.evidence: Aker BP reports turbine optimisation on Ula in 2024, confirming that the field centre generated operational power with gas turbines.

VALEMON.label: Host gas turbines
VALEMON.evidence: Kvitebjørn exported 15.18 GWh of electricity to Valemon in 2025; its electricity was generated mainly by gas-fired generator turbines, with zero imports from shore or offshore wind.

VALHALL.label: Power from shore
VALHALL.source_title: Fields with power to shore — Norwegian Offshore Directorate
VALHALL.evidence: SODIR states that Valhall's power-from-shore solution became operational in 2012 and covers the field's entire power need.

VARG.label: Gas / diesel engines
VARG.source_title: Annual report to the Norwegian Environment Agency for Varg 2016
VARG.evidence: Repsol's 2016 report lists four Wärtsilä 18V32GDLN dual-fuel main engines on Petrojarl Varg and reports both fuel-gas and diesel operation.

VESLEFRIKK.label: Gas turbine
VESLEFRIKK.evidence: Equinor's final full-year environmental report says electricity was mainly generated by generator turbines, records 29.5 million Sm3 of fuel gas burned in turbines, and reports no imported electricity from shore, wind, or another field.

VISUND.label: Gas turbine
VISUND.source_title: Norwegian Environment Agency operating permit for Visund
VISUND.evidence: The official permit identifies turbines and motors as Visund's energy plant and explicitly regulates gas consumption in its turbines, including a gas-fired low-NOx turbine.

VOLVE.label: Gas turbine + diesel
VOLVE.source_title: Yme New Development – Power from Shore
VOLVE.evidence: Volve produced from Mærsk Inspirer; Repsol's official study for that same unit documents two Solar Titan gas-turbine generators for the process module and four diesel generators for the rig and drilling systems.

YME.label: Gas turbine
YME.source_title: Repsol Norge 2023 Sustainability Plan and Year-end Report
YME.evidence: Repsol reports that Yme's plant can operate with one gas turbine together with lower-fuel-demand diesel generators, confirming gas-turbine-led offshore generation.

ÅSGARD.label: Gas turbine
ÅSGARD.evidence: Equinor's 2024 field report records fuel-gas turbine combustion and active DLE/SAC generator sources on both Åsgard A and Åsgard B.
